title: The Hollow of the Glass Steppe Again
premise: Gideon Crane, a mercenary bound to the silent god Vessel-of-Rains, has spent his life in the valley where magic cannot follow, believing his oath died with the god's voice. When the border wards collapse and the stars go out, he learns his god was never silent but imprisoned, and that the soul sold to the court beneath the mountain is his sister's, taken as payment for the oath itself. Gideon must cross the glass steppe, gather allies who each owe him differently, and bargain with the Undercourt before the thirteenth turn of the moon seals the bargain forever. He wins her soul back by surrendering his own memories of her, choosing justice outside any law and love that persists without recollection.
about_author: Jonah Lockridge is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping disputed borders before turning to fiction about people trapped by lines drawn by others. He writes in a converted lighthouse on the northern coast, where he claims the fog improves his prose.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. On watch at the valley's edge, Gideon watches the wards fail and the stars extinguish one by one, then finds a dying courier carrying a contract bearing his own name and his sister Wren's soul-price. The beat is dread: the safe world he guarded was always a cage.

chapters.title: What the God Left Behind
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Searching the abandoned shrine, he finds Vessel-of-Rains' last testament: the god traded its voice to buy Wren's soul back from the Undercourt once already, and the debt has come due again. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve as duty and love become the same thing.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Broken Roads
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A disgraced mapmaker who once charted the steppe agrees to guide Gideon, hiding that she sold the route's secrets to the Undercourt years ago. Beat: wary alliance; two people who both betrayed someone to survive recognize each other.

chapters.title: Salt and Thirteenth Moons
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Crossing the salt flats, the party meets Ovid, a priest of a rival god who offers passage in exchange for Gideon swearing to kill the Undercourt's regent. Beat: temptation—justice offered as a leash, and Gideon refusing to be anyone's weapon again.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They descend through the glass caves into the Undercourt, a place where memory is currency, and Sefa's old debts are called in publicly. Beat: humiliation and exposure; she confesses her betrayal to Gideon, testing whether trust can survive truth.

chapters.title: Wren, As She Is Now
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He finds Wren serving the regent, her soul fragmented into oaths she cannot break, and she does not want to leave—the court gave her purpose the valley never did. Beat: devastating reversal; rescue refused by the person being rescued.

chapters.title: The Regent's Bargain
chapters.summary: Regent Ilvane's POV. The regent reveals the thirteenth moon is her own doing—a clock built to force the gods to answer—and offers Gideon Wren's freedom if he takes his god's place beneath the mountain. Beat: seduction of sacrifice; every escape route leads deeper in.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Climax. As the moon completes its turn, Gideon refuses both bargains, instead invoking the original contract's flaw: the god bought Wren's soul once, so it was never truly the court's to sell. The court convulses; Ovid's forces attack; Sefa burns her maps to blind the regent. Beat: chaos, courage, cost.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The court accepts a substitute payment: not Gideon's life but his memories of Wren. He pays willingly while she screams at him not to, and walks out carrying a soul he no longer knows he saved. Beat: love against duty resolved—duty kept, love surrendered.

chapters.title: The Hollow Where Memory Was
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, ending on Wren's. Back in the valley under returning stars, Wren tends Gideon, a stranger who feels like home, and begins telling him their story piece by piece. Beat: bittersweet resolution—memory lost but love rebuilt, justice achieved by no law but their own.
